- **muskarch**: Elon Musk acquired Twitter for $44 billion in October 2022. The acquisition financing included $1 billion from Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund (Public Investment Fund), $250M from Qatar's sovereign wealth fund, and contributions from other investors including Oracle's Larry Ellison ($1B) and Sequoia Capital. Saudi Arabia — whose government murdered journalist Jamal Khashoggi — is a co-owner of the platform Musk describes as essential to free speech. The SEC sued Musk in January 2025, alleging he violated securities law by failing to disclose his Twitter stock purchases within the required 10-day window, allowing him to buy additional shares at artificially low prices and saving an estimated $150M. The case was later dropped by the Trump-era SEC.
- **oligarchy**: Because loans are not taxable income, wealthy individuals can borrow substantial sums against their appreciated (but unsold) assets to fund living expenses, avoiding a taxable sale entirely. ProPublica's reporting documented specific, named instances: Oracle's Larry Ellison secured a credit line against $10 billion of Oracle stock; Elon Musk pledged 92 million Tesla shares, then worth over $50 billion, to secure personal loans; Carl Icahn held loans including a $1.2 billion line from Bank of America. [cite:atf_stepped_up_basis] This strategy is commonly called 'buy, borrow, die' — buy appreciating assets, borrow against them tax-free instead of selling, and hold until death, at which point the next entity in this scene applies.
